races.name: Book Tickets Online At www.corkracecourse.ie Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Aiteall
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist trained by Joseph O'Brien, finishing flag is a concern given the fade warning, but the 10-day turnaround is sharp and three recent runs on similar Good ground bring zero wins or placings — needs everything to go right.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Aiteall faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's distance and going before and comes back quickly enough on just ten days' rest.

runners_data.name: Glamazon
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's hold-up filly has placed 4 times from 13 runs on Good and shaped well at 8f on similar surfaces; the 7lb apprentice Darragh O'Sullivan could be an asset navigating a messy straight if she gets room.
runners_data.comment: Glamazon shaped well with a third last time out, and her experience over today's distance and going stands her in good stead from stall three carrying 142 lb; a rating of 70 marks her as the one to beat here, though consistency has been her Achilles heel in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Dawn Flame
runners_data.note: Paul Flynn's hold-up filly has placed at 7f and 8f on Good, giving her proven form at the trip and surface; the fade note is absent and her consistent place record makes her one of the more straightforward closers in the field.
runners_data.comment: Dawn Flame has run over today's trip and going, and his recent placed efforts — third two starts back and third four starts back — suggest he is knocking on the door, returning fit after just 16 days; yet to score in recent starts and a trainer striking at just 5% are the chief concerns.

runners_data.name: Oppenheimer
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from Kevin Coleman's yard with a quiet recent record over shorter trips on Good and Soft; stepping to a mile for the first time may help but six runs on sim going without a win or place is a red flag.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Oppenheimer nonetheless catches the eye on conditions — he has run over today's trip and going before, and a 23-day break looks a freshening spell, with our rating of 69 suggesting he is ahead of his official mark of 59.

runners_data.name: Sunrise Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer for Andrew Slattery with two placed efforts on Good from nine sim-going runs; no fade flag but the 23-day absence and consistent mid-to-back finishes leave her dependent on a clean passage in a crowded straight.
runners_data.comment: Sunrise Angel has run over today's trip and going, and our rating puts him third among 16 rivals, marking him out as a leading threat; the worry is that he has been winless in his last five starts, with two sixths among recent efforts.

runners_data.name: Tenacious
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's 3yo is a genuine hold-up horse by nature but the field density forces her into a midfield map slot she would not naturally choose — her fade flag and 0-from-10 on similar going ask serious questions of her finishing effort.
runners_data.comment: Tenacious arrives here winless in her last six starts and has looked disappointing in recent outings, though a third five starts back offers a flicker of encouragement; she has run over today's trip and going, and returns after a 15-day break carrying 135 lb from stall 15.

runners_data.name: Beau Army
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner for Adrian McGuinness, with a win over 7f on Good and a placed effort at 8f; the visor is on, the draw and lack of pace rivals give him every chance to dictate, though the Style_Fit flag notes a slight role compromise as a nominally prominent rather than pure lead horse.
runners_data.comment: Beau Army was a winner two starts back but has since disappointed with a fourth, and while she has run over today's distance and going before, her official rating of 52 and ranking eighth of sixteen suggest she faces a stiff ask from 134 lb out of stall four.

runners_data.name: Ochtar Againn
runners_data.note: M J Byrne's hold-up filly is genuinely a closer by nature but will be shuffled into midfield by sheer field volume — four runs on similar going without a place and a 0-from-8 sim-going record make her hard to fancy regardless of where she ends up.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with unplaced efforts dotted throughout that recent sequence, Ochtar Againn is hard to fancy from stall 12 carrying 134 lb, though she has run over today's distance and going before and comes here on a reasonable 23-day break.

runners_data.name: Sceitimini
runners_data.note: Rodger Sweeney's hold-up type has all five recent career starts over 5f-6f, so this mile trip is a significant test of stamina; the fade flag compounds the trip concern, and her true hold-up style is masked by the redistribution into midfield.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Sceitimini has at least shown experience over today's trip and conditions, though a fifth and an eighth among recent efforts tell their own story; carrying 134 lb from stall 11, he looks a tough nut to crack at this level.

runners_data.name: Miss Ivor
runners_data.note: P O'Rourke's hold-up filly has never finished better than 8th in her last five starts, all on Good or similar; the fade flag, a 23-day break, and the fact she is a natural backmarker pressed forward by the pack shape all weigh against her.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts with a string of unplaced efforts, Miss Ivor faces a stiff task from a rating of 50 in a field of 16, though she has run over today's trip and going and returns on a reasonable 23-day break.

runners_data.name: Sayonara
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's prominent-style runner has a previous placed effort at 7f and is one of only two horses genuinely suited to racing close to Beau Army; an OR of 51 and five runs on similar going with one placing makes her the obvious travelling companion to the leader.
runners_data.comment: Sayonara has run over today's trip and going before and shaped with promise when second last time out, yet he remains winless in his last six starts and that inconsistency — including two unplaced efforts in recent form — is the concern from stall ten carrying 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Arizona Star
runners_data.note: Michael Mulvany's horse is a genuine hold-up type placed on Good ground over 10f but nudged into midfield by field density — the 53-day absence is the most significant layoff in the field and casts doubt over her readiness despite the placed form.
runners_data.comment: Arizona Star is winless in her last five starts, and ranked thirteenth of sixteen on our figures, making her hard to fancy; she does return with distance and going experience, and her third last time out offers a crumb of encouragement, but the 53-day absence and stall 16 add further question marks.

runners_data.name: Cause I Like You
runners_data.note: A true closer with genuine winning form at 8f on Good — the most relevant winning profile in the field for this trip and surface — but the redistribution into midfield means Wesley Joyce will need to find room to express that finishing kick in a congested straight.
runners_data.comment: Cause I Like You won two starts back and filled second three starts back, showing she can mix it at this level, but a fifth last time out and 131 lb from stall 14 are obstacles, though she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Thumama Sands
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness's hold-up 3yo is 0-from-4 on similar going, all at 7f and shorter, and now faces a mile; the fade tag and 36-day absence make her profile among the most vulnerable in the field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Thumama Sands does at least bring distance and going experience to this, and a 36-day break may have freshened him up, though a mark of 49 and draw nine make this a stiff ask from 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Due In June
runners_data.note: Ian Donoghue's hold-up filly has five runs on Good at distances up to 8f without a win or place, the fade flag is present, and 59 days off is the longest break in the field — the combination of layoff, form, and natural style disadvantage is significant.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last five starts and off for 59 days, Due In June faces a stiff ask from 130 lb out of stall one, though she has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 58 offers a sliver of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Garryowen Green
runners_data.note: Andrew McNamara's lowest-rated runner in the field (OR 40) has placed at 7f on Good but carries the fade flag; a genuine closer by nature forced into the midfield cluster, and the Class gap to OR 60 rivals is the biggest hurdle to overcome.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked fourteenth of sixteen on our figures, Garryowen Green is hard to fancy, though a third last time out offers a crumb of comfort and he has run over today's distance and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Beau Army is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-runner field and, with no natural rival for the lead, should be able to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Yielding ground at Cork. Sayonara is the only other horse with a prominent tag and may track closely, but the remainder of the field — Tenacious, Sceitimini, Ochtar Againn, Miss Ivor, Arizona Star, Cause I Like You, Thumama Sands, Due In June, and Garryowen Green — are all genuine hold-up types redistributed into midfield slots because the field cannot accommodate them at the rear simultaneously; in reality, several of these will be forced to race closer than they want. The pace dynamic is one of a single, uncontested front-runner setting a measured tempo in front of a congested midfield mass, which means Beau Army will be allowed a soft lead with minimal pressure through the first half-mile. This shape squarely favours hold-up horses who can find a clear run from the back of the middle pack and use the strong late finish that a steady-tempo-led race over a mile on a soft-ish surface encourages — but with so many closers competing for the same late ground, getting a clear passage will be the defining tactical factor.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Beau Army Leads Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Beau Army is allowed to control a steady fractions race and the hold-up pack fails to find clear daylight in time.
scenarios.body: Beau Army dictates every yard from a low draw at a comfortable clip, and the hold-up wall behind him gets tangled in traffic as the field converges on the home turn; Sayonara tracks just off the pace in the ideal seat and is best placed to challenge as the field switches off the rail.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Split The Field
scenarios.trigger: If a runner from the hold-up pack finds a seam of daylight entering the straight and picks up strongly on the Good to Yielding surface.
scenarios.body: A moderate pace set by Beau Army sets up the race for a horse with a strong late kick, and a well-positioned hold-up runner who avoids the inevitable traffic bunching gets a clean run to mow down the leader; Glamazon's record of placing on Good ground at 8f makes her the profile fit, while Cause I Like You's proven winning form over this trip and ground suits.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Hotts Up Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If Sayonara or multiple prominent-type horses rediscover competitive instincts and push the tempo in the middle of the race, lifting fractions.
scenarios.body: Redistributed hold-up horses are forced even further back than comfortable as the early pace quickens, stringing the field out and turning this into a genuine test of stamina over the mile on yielding ground; a genuine stayer who gets room late, such as Dawn Flame with proven placed efforts at 7f-8f on Good, could emerge from the pack to finish powerfully.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Hands It Front
scenarios.trigger: If the bunched midfield fails to disentangle throughout the straight and the field's closers collectively block one another.
scenarios.body: Beau Army and Sayonara steal the race from the front as the congested hold-up pack never gets a clean enough run to mount a coordinated challenge; this is the least desirable shape for the majority of runners but most beneficial for the two horses racing closest to their natural position.

watchPoints.text: Beau Army has a completely clear lead with no natural pace rival — watch whether Sam Coen uses this to conserve energy for a kick in the final furlong or gets swept up by first-time vying from Sayonara.

The bunched midfield of redistributed hold-up horses creates a serious traffic flashpoint entering the home turn — watch for Cause I Like You and Glamazon specifically trying to find an outside route to avoid the jam.

Sayonara at OR 51 is the only horse naturally suited to tracking Beau Army; if she travels smoothly just off the pace she carries a place threat disproportionate to her rating — watch how Adam Browne-Souza positions her in the first two furlongs.

Dawn Flame drops back from shorter trips in recent starts but her placed form at 8f suggests the mile suits — watch whether Reese Holohan attempts to avoid the inner crush by angling wide early in the straight.

Cause I Like You has won over this exact trip and surface profile but faces the challenge of racing out of her natural deep-held position — watch whether Wesley Joyce commits to an earlier move than usual to avoid being shut in by the field.

races.name: Glenvale Stud Race

runners_data.name: Benevento
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits the predicted race shape; W J Lee takes the ride for Robson De Aguiar on his preferred 7f trip, and recent form (including a win at 8f on Good) suggests he travels well — the crowded prominent group is the main tactical hazard.|
runners_data.comment: Benevento won last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, making him a clear danger at 140 lb from stall five; the main risk is whether that weight blunts his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Felix Guido
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in three before a flat 10th last time (125 days off), this Joseph O'Brien three-year-old showed early speed but the flagged tendency to fade in the finish is a major concern at 7f on Good To Yielding; the long absence and single similar-going run add further uncertainty.|
runners_data.comment: Felix Guido returns after 125 days off the track, and our rating of 62 ranks him eighth of nine in this field, making him difficult to fancy despite a lively recent record that includes three wins in his last four starts; he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Bold Style
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type for Andrew Slattery, who both trains and rides, showing modest recent form (best of 3rd, 6th, and 11th in last five); the Good To Yielding surface is fine, but a late run depends entirely on the pace collapsing — an unlikely scenario here.|
runners_data.comment: Bold Style returns after 48 days without a win in his last five starts, though that third last time out shows a flicker of form worth noting; he has run over today's trip and going before, and carries 136 lb from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Gleneagle Bay
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a strong course profile (12 from 15 runs on similar going), Jack Kearney claiming 3lb is useful, and the six-year-old won over 7f at Gowran on Good last season; needs genuine pace to exploit his finishing kick, making Scenario A slightly uncomfortable but Scenario C his ideal race.|
runners_data.comment: Gleneagle Bay won three starts back and arrives here fit on a 28-day turnaround, with experience of both today's trip and going working in his favour at 136 lb from stall eight; the concern is that he has finished sixth in each of his last two outings.

runners_data.name: Inventor
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse who last ran 847 days ago, returning for Gillian Scott with minimal recent stable confidence (0 from 2 in 14 days); the redistribution to midfield reflects that the rear is congested, not that his style has changed, and the extended absence makes meaningful contribution here very unlikely regardless of position.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and off the track for over two years, Inventor faces a steep ask back here, though he has run over today's distance and going before and carries a manageable 136 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Bamako Beach
runners_data.note: Progressive three-year-old with a win and two runner-up finishes in four similar-going starts; Seamie Heffernan is a strong booking for M D O'Callaghan, and the horse's ability to settle prominently and finish strongly — evidenced at 7f on Good — makes this race shape a natural fit.|
runners_data.comment: Bamako Beach arrives on the back of a win last time out, with experience of today's distance and going counting in his favour, and he merits respect as the top-rated runner here despite a 53-day absence; carry 135 lb from stall 6.

runners_data.name: Res Ipsa
runners_data.note: The lone front runner, proven at 8f on Good for G M Lyons and Colin Keane, who can control tempo from the front; if permitted to roll along unchallenged she is the primary pace-setter and a genuine winning threat, though dropping back to 7f from 8f is worth noting.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well below his rivals on our figures, Res Ipsa is hard to fancy despite a win and two seconds in his last four starts; he has run over today's trip and going, and the 48-day break gives him every chance to show up fresh.

runners_data.name: Roaring Fire
runners_data.note: High-rated (OR 120) but one-run wonder who won over 6f on Soft for M D O'Callaghan 346 days ago; wants a prominent berth and Jamie Powell takes the ride, but unknown stamina reserves at 7f and the very long absence make this a horse of significant uncertainty despite the talent the OR implies.|
runners_data.comment: Roaring Fire comes here on the back of a win last time out, which is the obvious plus, but he has been off the track for 346 days and that lengthy absence is the key question mark; the 135 lb burden will not help either.

runners_data.name: Bella Isabella
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from the powerful D K Weld yard with Chris Hayes aboard; has won at 7f on Soft and placed on Good, so the surface is fine, but needs a truly run race over this trip to deploy her finishing effort — the controlled pace scenario makes her task harder than her form suggests.|
runners_data.comment: Bella Isabella brings winning form to this, successful two starts back, and she has run over today's trip and going before; the chief concern is her latest fifth on a comeback after 52 days, though 131 lb from stall 1 keeps her firmly in the mix.

races.paceDynamic: Res Ipsa is the lone confirmed front runner and, with Colin Keane in the saddle for G M Lyons, is expected to control affairs from the off at a sustainable, unforced tempo over this 7f trip on Good To Yielding ground. Behind her, Benevento, Felix Guido, Bamako Beach, and Roaring Fire all want prominent positions, creating a compressed, contested cluster in the first two furlongs that carries genuine traffic risk between the 2f and 3f markers. Bold Style, Gleneagle Bay, Bella Isabella, and the redistributed Inventor make up the back section, though Inventor is a natural hold-up type who is unlikely to find clear daylight from an unfavoured map position in this shape. With pace controlled rather than pressured, this race shape favours horses that can travel prominently behind a lone front runner and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — prominent types with a strong finishing record on similar ground, particularly Bamako Beach and Roaring Fire, are the primary beneficiaries, while true hold-up horses face a stiff challenge if the pace does not genuinely collapse the field late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Res Ipsa Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Res Ipsa dictates a steady-to-moderate tempo unchallenged and the prominent pack settles cleanly behind her.
scenarios.body: Res Ipsa sets a manageable gallop, allowing the prominent group to travel sweetly and unload their finishing kick from two furlongs out; the Good To Yielding surface rewards horses with class and stamina rather than pure sprint speed, suiting those who have settled well in the slipstream.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Leader Outstays
scenarios.trigger: If the congested prominent group creates early friction and burns pace, leaving Res Ipsa to stride clear as rivals tire.
scenarios.body: The contest for positions behind Res Ipsa generates more sustained pressure than anticipated, and Res Ipsa — who has already run prominently and placed on similar going — benefits from rivals wasting energy in a mid-pack scuffle; Colin Keane, a supreme judge of pace, can then extend the advantage into the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely hot enough to string the field out and create a strong sectional finish for closers.
scenarios.body: Gleneagle Bay or Bella Isabella, both proven hold-up types on similar going, would need a contested gallop to manufacture the gaps required at 7f; the surface is capable of rewarding late runners if the early tempo is misjudged, but the lone front runner scenario makes this contingency less likely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Capitalises on Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If early positional fighting causes multiple rivals to lose their rhythm and an overlooked runner threads through.
scenarios.body: Roaring Fire, with just one run to their name and a high OR of 120, carries unknown stamina reserves at 7f that could be unlocked by chaotic early fractions; an extreme scenario, but the combination of long absence (346 days) and raw ability means an upset cannot be entirely discounted if conditions fall perfectly.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion in the opening furlongs is severe — Benevento, Felix Guido, Bamako Beach, and Roaring Fire all want to sit just behind Res Ipsa, and a check or bump between the 1f and 2f marks could stop several of them cold.
Roaring Fire's 346-day absence and unproven stamina at 7f means Jamie Powell must manage an unknown quantity — if the horse jumps keenly or over-races early, his chance evaporates quickly.

Felix Guido's flagged tendency to fade in the finish combined with a 125-day layoff makes him a significant risk for punters expecting his early-career form to translate — monitor whether he is firmly on the bridle mid-race.

Inventor's 847-day absence and redistribution to midfield despite a hold-up profile means he is highly unlikely to factor — any market support should be treated with caution as his true form profile is entirely misaligned with how this race is expected to be run.

Res Ipsa steps down from 8f to 7f — if Keane elects to press on slightly faster than typical to compensate for the shorter trip, it could unintentionally benefit the prominent group travelling just behind her.

races.name: Coolmore Stud Little Big Bear Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Catalina Delcarpio
runners_data.note: Prominent racer stepping back from a disappointing 12f run to a more natural 7f trip; P Twomey has been quiet (0/13 in 14 days) but this mare has strong form at 7-8f on good ground, and 74 days off may see her fresh; runner-up on good ground last season suggests she stays involved late.
runners_data.comment: Catalina Delcarpio showed real quality when winning two starts back, and with experience over today's trip and going she arrives as a genuine threat; the main concern is a 74-day absence and an unplaced effort on her most recent outing.

runners_data.name: Greydreambeliever
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at 7f but a true hold-up type whose redistribution into midfield on this map reflects genuine traffic concerns; the visor is a notable addition, and sim-going form (14/15) shows she handles conditions, but Scott McCullagh will need a race that truly falls apart up front for her to land a blow from where she'll likely be.

runners_data.name: Princess Child
runners_data.note: A strong hold-up finisher who showed ability when second over this trip in good-to-yielding conditions but has posted some disappointing runs recently including consecutive 11th-place finishes; the tongue-tie is noted and she handles this going, but getting a clean run from the rear in a 14-runner field at Cork is far from guaranteed.
runners_data.comment: Ranked second of 14 runners on our ratings, Princess Child brings strong claims on her form, with a second four starts back and experience of today's trip and going; the risk is that she has been winless in her last five starts, with two unplaced efforts most recently.

runners_data.name: Stugardia
runners_data.note: Returning from 329 days off which is a significant query; suited by soft ground based on all five recent runs coming on that surface, but good-to-yielding is likely faster than ideal; Joseph O'Brien has multiple runners here and Nathan Crosse takes the ride — one to watch in running rather than bet on blind.
runners_data.comment: Stugardia is a filly who returns after 329 days off the track with her form showing a third two starts back, and she remains lightly raced and open to significant improvement; yet to win in recent starts, she carries 133 lb from stall two.

runners_data.name: Wannabe Royal
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on good ground last August which is a solid form line; eight-place run last time out on soft is forgettable and 80 days off sets the freshness angle; Ronan Whelan knows her well and she should find a prominent position behind Suzie Songs, but her tendency to just miss in weaker races is a concern at this level.
runners_data.comment: Wannabe Royal won two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, with 133 lb from stall 11 her only real query alongside the 80-day absence; she arrives with strong credentials to go close.

runners_data.name: Cromac Quay
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced three-year-old who has won his last run over 7f on soft ground and placed twice before that; Shane Foley takes over which is an upgrade, and the upward form trajectory on just three starts makes him interesting; the step into Group company is the obvious concern but he could outrun his odds if pace suits prominent runners.
runners_data.comment: Cromac Quay arrives on the back of a run of form that reads well enough — third, second, then a win — but she is ranked a long way down our figures in a field of 14, and an 80-day absence adds to the concerns despite having experience of today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Dancing Saxon
runners_data.note: Rattled off three wins from four starts and was a credible third last week, confirming he is in the form of his life; Declan McDonogh is an astute jockey for a tactical race like this, and the horse's ability to win from just off the pace at 7f on good ground is directly relevant; the one-day turnaround after a recent run is short but O'Brien clearly has him spot-on.
runners_data.comment: Consistent recent form sees Dancing Saxon arrive here on the back of a third last time out, having won two starts back, and her record of three wins in her last five starts speaks to her quality, though carrying 128 lb from stall 13 may test her, and experience over today's trip and going at least holds no fears.

runners_data.name: Josh's Joy
runners_data.note: Prominent-style three-year-old who has not run for 105 days, and while he has won over 7f on good ground his form over 6f trips suggests he may prefer slightly shorter; Chris Hayes will aim to find a handy position but the layoff and the step into Group 3 company at this trip are genuine questions.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 14 on our figures, Josh's Joy arrives 105 days between runs and has finished fifth and seventh in her last two starts, making her hard to fancy despite a win three starts back and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Magny Cours
runners_data.note: Three consecutive placed efforts at 7f including runner-up finishes on good and similar ground suggest he is consistent and versatile; Ben Coen is a strong jockey booking and the horse handles good-to-yielding well (8/9 sim-going), but a last-time-out tenth-place finish on good ground at a similar level is a slight concern about this specific ground or trip combination.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts but has placed four times in that sequence, with a second two starts back and a second three starts back among them; she has run over today's distance and going before, though 98 days off the track is a fitness query at 128 lb from stall eight.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Attack
runners_data.note: Won nicely over 7f on soft ground (1st) with three placed efforts at this trip; the alarming note is that he ran only yesterday, which even for a fit horse is an extraordinary ask in a Group 3 two days running; Seamie Heffernan takes the ride but freshness must be a genuine query and the trainer has been quiet at 0/5 in 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Pivotal Attack won two starts back and, with experience over today's trip and going, she arrives as the top-rated runner in the field; the single-day turnaround is the one note of caution, but 128 lb from stall 12 represents a workable ask.

runners_data.name: Prevalence
runners_data.note: Won twice including over 7f on standard ground for G M Lyons and Colin Keane retains the ride, a strong booking; this is a genuine hold-up type pushed into midfield by the crowded rear of the race shape, so his finishes may be blunted by the inability to get clear daylight — Keane will need to be patient and creative to deliver him off what may be a falsely slow gallop.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom two on our figures and rated 4 lb below her official mark, Prevalence is hard to fancy despite a mixed recent record that does include a win last time out and a third three starts back; the 65-day absence adds another question mark.

runners_data.name: Spinning Around
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse based on history who has won over this 7f trip; the tongue-tie is noted and Gavin Ryan is a capable jockey, but Donnacha O'Brien running multiple hold-up types here means they will get in each other's way and Spinning Around is unlikely to find the clean passage her style demands, moderately discounting her chance in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up sixteen days ago shows she retains form, but she has struggled to recapture that sole recent victory, finishing fifth and eighth in between; experience over today's trip and going helps, though carrying 128 lb from stall six keeps expectations measured.

runners_data.name: Suzie Songs
runners_data.note: Cork 7f specialist with back-to-back wins on this exact track and trip; lone confirmed front-runner here who faces zero pressure for the lead, giving Gary Carroll a dream tactical opportunity on good-to-yielding; consistent going record (8/8 on similar) and recent 16-day turnaround is well within Lyons' yard pattern.
runners_data.comment: Suzie Songs arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and 16 days is a sharp enough turnaround to suggest she retains her form, though a fourth and two disappointing efforts earlier in this sequence are a reminder she can be inconsistent; she has run over today's trip and going before and carries 128 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Wild Bessie
runners_data.note: Won over 7f at The Curragh on good-to-yielding ground which is directly relevant form; Wayne Lordan is an experienced hand but this horse's four-runner similar-going record shows limited reach (2/4), and as a redistributed hold-up type without a clear run materialising late at Cork, she will need this race to fall apart spectacularly in front of her.
runners_data.comment: Wild Bessie won three starts back but has since posted a seventh and an unplaced effort, and ranked tenth of fourteen on our figures she looks up against it here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 46 days between runs at least means she arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Suzie Songs is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field and, critically, faces no genuine rival willing to press her for the lead — Catalina Delcarpio, Wannabe Royal, Cromac Quay, Pivotal Attack and Josh's Joy will contest the prominent positions but none is a natural gate-to-wire type, meaning Suzie Songs should settle into a controlled, uncontested lead on good-to-yielding ground at Cork. The pace she sets will therefore be sustainable and rhythm-controlled rather than suicidal, giving her every chance to dictate terms and quicken away from the field entering the straight. Behind her, the prominent-style runners will jostle for the best seats in behind, while several genuine hold-up horses — Spinning Around, Prevalence, Greydreambeliever and Wild Bessie — are redistributed into midfield on the map because the rear of the field is already saturated with hold-up types who cannot all get the gap they need; their true late-running profiles are compromised by the traffic situation this race shape will create. This race shape strongly favours the lone front-runner and, as a secondary benefit, horses with the tactical speed to sit second or third and track Suzie Songs through the race, because the lack of pressure up front and the crowded hold-up group make late closers vulnerable to a wall of horses ahead of them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Suzie Songs Controls Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Suzie Songs leads without any rival attempting to press her pace, settles comfortably and has enough in reserve to extend from the front in the straight.
scenarios.body: Suzie Songs has won back-to-back on this exact course and distance on good ground and faces no credible challenger for the lead here; on a flat, right-handed Cork track over 7f with good-to-yielding underfoot, an uncontested front-runner who can control the tempo has a major structural advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Suzie Songs sets a proper pace and a horse sitting second or third tracks her through the race before asserting in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Catalina Delcarpio or Cromac Quay, tucked in behind Suzie Songs and travelling sweetly, is best placed to pick up when the leader ties up late; Dancing Saxon's consistent recent form and jockey Declan McDonogh's tactical awareness make him a live candidate to swoop from just off the pace with a clean run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Splits Field
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops false pace early and a horse from midfield sustains a powerful run through the centre of the track to pick off tiring rivals.
scenarios.body: Magny Cours or Princess Child, both capable of finishing powerfully through a gap, could benefit if the prominent group burn each other out chasing Suzie Songs; however this scenario is constrained by the fact that Cork's 7f flat configuration rarely sets up for dramatic late closers, and the sustainable pace Suzie Songs is likely to set further undermines it.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses badly in the straight and genuine hold-up horses get a clear passage to finish powerfully through a tired field.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on Spinning Around, Prevalence or Greydreambeliever running to their true hold-up style — but all three are redistributed from the rear on the map, meaning they are unlikely to find the clear passage or separation from the pack they would need; the probability is materially discounted because the race shape actively works against these horses securing their natural position.

watchPoints.text: Suzie Songs leads uncontested — if Gary Carroll gets her into a clean rhythm without being forced wide from the draw or bumped at the start, she is structurally very hard to peg back; watch whether any prominent rival challenges her before the final turn.

Pivotal Attack ran just one day ago — watch the pre-race and early stages closely; if he shows any distress in the paddock or is ridden with uncharacteristic restraint, it signals Heffernan is nursing a horse well short of peak freshness and the stable run should be dismissed.

Dancing Saxon is running for the third time in a short period but arrived here in winning form and Declan McDonogh will target the rail position second or third — if he gets that berth behind Suzie Songs without being shuffled back in the early jostle among the prominent group, he becomes the most dangerous pressing rival.

The multiple O'Brien runners (Greydreambeliever, Princess Child, Stugardia, Dancing Saxon, Spinning Around) create potential for interference mid-race; watch whether jockeys are issued separate orders or whether a clear stable number one emerges from the parade ring — Dancing Saxon's recent form and jockey suggests he is the de facto lead runner.

Cork 7f good-to-yielding conditions place a premium on relaxed early travel and strong finishing — any horse that is fractious in the stalls or wastes energy in the first two furlongs against a slow Suzie Songs tempo will have little left when the race quickens entering the final two furlongs.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Abergwaun Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Kendall Roy
runners_data.note: Won at 5f on Good last time and has three wins from six attempts on similar going at this trip, giving him a strong profile for today; tracks prominently and Colin Hayes will look to slot just off Rosie Frith's shoulder — the prime tactical position in this shape.|
runners_data.comment: Kendall Roy shaped well when third two starts back and brings proven fitness on 22 days' rest, while his experience over today's trip and going bolsters his claims at 136 lb from stall three; the concern is that last-time-out sixth suggests he needs to find improvement.

runners_data.name: Erosandpsyche
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up specialist whose best runs at 5f on Good going — including two places from six attempts — suggest he needs the race to develop a gap; Gary Carroll will be patient but needs a clean run late.|
runners_data.comment: Erosandpsyche shaped with promise when second three starts back, and his experience over today's distance and going gives him a solid grounding here off 133 lb from stall six; the risk is a tendency to disappoint, with two eighths in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Brussels
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien three-year-old who has shown up prominently in his recent starts, but form figures of 19-5-12-4-6 at 5-6f reveal inconsistency and he steps down in grade here; likely to press the early pace but his ability to sustain it on soft-leaning ground is uncertain.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Brussels nevertheless heads the ratings here and steps back onto familiar distance and going, with 30 days between runs suggesting he arrives fresh; the 131 lb burden is the chief question mark.

runners_data.name: Gazelle d'Or
runners_data.note: Freshest horse in the field at 86 days off, with two runner-up finishes at 5-6f on Good in her last four completed starts; naturally races off the pace but has shown she can deliver a consistent late effort — course freshness is a risk, not a given.|
runners_data.comment: Gazelle d'Or arrives with strong each-way claims, back-to-back runner-up efforts highlighting her consistency, and she has run over today's distance and going before; the main concern is a lengthy 86-day absence, and she remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Likedbymike
runners_data.note: Won over 6f at Cork last time and comes back to 5f on preferred Good ground; Colin Keane's booking is a strong positive, and his front-three positioning makes him one of the best-placed runners to exploit the tracking role in this pace scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Likedbymike won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her solid claims, though her form in recent starts has been inconsistent, mixing a third and a second with an unplaced effort, and she carries 128 lb from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Sarahmae
runners_data.note: Three wins on soft-leaning or soft ground but the recent form figures of 6-5-6 are concerning — she's a hold-up type who needs a flawless run and a faltering pace to land a blow at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Sarahmae has experience of today's trip and going, and her two wins in her last six starts show she can find the line — a second four starts back and a winner five starts back hint at ability — but three consecutive finishes of sixth, fifth, and sixth in recent starts are the concern, and she carries 128 lb from stall two.

runners_data.name: Cardiff By The Sea
runners_data.note: Trainer J A Stack also saddles Focaccia; a 57-day absence is worth noting, and while naturally a front-running/prominent type, the congested early order means she is unlikely to find her preferred position — the style-fit discount is real and her chance depends on a cleaner-than-expected break.|
runners_data.comment: A winner four starts back, Cardiff By The Sea has struggled for consistency since, finishing fifth last time out and seventh two starts back, and her 57-day absence adds a fitness query; she has run over today's trip and going, and draws stall one carrying 126 lb.

runners_data.name: Focaccia
runners_data.note: Only seven days since last run suggests fitness, but the form string of 7-8-2-8-6 at 5-6f shows rare moments of quality; like stablemate Cardiff By The Sea, her natural prominence will be frustrated by the busy early order and she'll likely race further back than suits.|
runners_data.comment: Focaccia has finished sixth and eighth in her last two starts, and sits bottom of our rankings for this field, making her hard to fancy at the weights; a second three starts back offers some hope, as does experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Rosie Frith
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner in the field with a winning strike rate of three wins from recent 5f starts on Good; Shane Foley takes the ride for Patrick Magee and she has every chance to dictate terms uncontested — the key question is whether the ground is fast enough to maintain her advantage to the line.|
runners_data.comment: Rated 7 lb below her official mark on our figures and ranked eighth of ten, Rosie Frith is hard to fancy despite winning last time out; she has run over today's trip and going before, but a fourth two starts back and another fourth three starts back leave the overall profile unconvincing.

runners_data.name: Xerling
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on Good and has three placed efforts from seven in similar conditions; Ben Coen likely to push for a prominent pitch alongside the other jostling runners, but the traffic danger two-to-three out is the primary threat to his chance.|
runners_data.comment: Xerling ranks ninth of ten on our figures and arrives on the back of an unplaced run, making her hard to fancy despite a second two starts back and a win three starts back; she has run over today's trip and going, and her draw in stall five is noted.

races.paceDynamic: Rosie Frith is the confirmed front-runner and, with only one genuine leader in a field of ten at 5f on Good to Yielding ground, she is set to control tempo without being seriously pressured for the early lead. However, there is meaningful congestion immediately behind her — Kendall Roy, Brussels, Likedbymike, and Xerling all want prominent positions, creating a scrappy, jostling early phase across the first two furlongs that will cost energy and could generate brief checking movements two-to-three out. Cardiff By The Sea and Focaccia are natural prominent racers who, given the crowded middle-order, are unlikely to get within their comfort zone and will be shuffled further back than ideal. At 5f on soft-leaning ground with a single, uncontested pace-setter who can dictate without being harassed, this race shape strongly favours runners who can track Rosie Frith at close range in second or third — the prominent-to-tracking profile is the prime position, with a legitimate lead-and-last chance if the pace is misjudged — and the congested prominent group means true hold-up horses will need an exceptionally clean passage to land late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Controls, Tracks Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Rosie Frith establishes a comfortable rhythm unchallenged and the field is spread wide enough to allow clean tracking runs.
scenarios.body: Rosie Frith sets a measured, honest gallop that neither burns out nor dawdles, allowing the closest pursuers in second and third to quicken off her back in the final furlong; the prominent trackers — Kendall Roy and Likedbymike — are best placed to exploit this shape as they maintain cover and strike inside the last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Traffic Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the early congestion among Brussels, Kendall Roy, Likedbymike, and Xerling causes interference and disrupts their rhythm, leaving the race less settled.
scenarios.body: The scrappy early exchanges burn off the cruising speed of those jostling for position, meaning the race opens up in the final two furlongs for a horse who finds daylight late; Erosandpsyche or Gazelle d'Or, genuine hold-up types who avoid early trouble, are most likely to pick up the pieces from further back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Outstays Rivals
scenarios.trigger: If Rosie Frith produces a perfectly-judged front-running display and the field — congested and energy-sapped by early jostling — fails to close.
scenarios.body: The soft-leaning ground rewards a horse who can husband stamina from the front, and Rosie Frith's recent course-winning form and two wins from four at 5f on Good give her the profile to sustain the run-in; none of the prominent runners have enough residual energy to reel her in if she has two lengths in hand at the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Override
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically after early crowding and the race turns into a sprint finish off a strong early burn.
scenarios.body: A complete scenario breakdown — where the entire prominent and pace-setting group ties up — would theoretically open the door for Sarahmae or Erosandpsyche to finish over the top; however, this depends on conditions deteriorating sharply and genuine closers are scarce in this field, making it the least supported shape.

watchPoints.text: Rosie Frith to be monitored out of the gates — if she misses the break even marginally, the congested prominent group (Kendall Roy, Brussels, Likedbymike, Xerling) could swamp her and fundamentally reshape the pace dynamic.

The cluster of four prominent runners — Kendall Roy, Brussels, Likedbymike, and Xerling — racing for two or three positions directly off the leader creates a genuine interference flashpoint two-to-three furlongs out; any checking or bumping will cost the affected horse materially on soft-leaning ground.

Cardiff By The Sea and Focaccia, both natural front-runners for J A Stack, are at risk of racing too far off their natural rhythm if the prominent group is locked up ahead of them — watch for either to be caught wide or without cover early.

Gazelle d'Or's 86-day absence is the longest in the field; W J Lee will need an immediate clean run from the hold-up position — any hesitation after the stalls open could leave her with an impossible amount of ground to make up over just 5f.|

Erosandpsyche runs just 11 days after his last start and has now failed to win in six recent attempts, but his consistent placing at 5f on Good means he remains a live each-way danger if the pace quickens and gaps appear late.|

races.name: Cork Maiden

runners_data.name: Carry The Dream
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for W P Browne who faded on seasonal reappearance over 8f at Navan, and 49 days off may sharpen but this trip is likely too sharp for a horse that already struggles to sustain its effort late

runners_data.name: Hurleys Hill
runners_data.note: Patrick Flynn's hold-up type is only 15 days since a modest effort at Navan and has no obvious indication of improvement, while a tendency to fade in the finish makes a strongly-run 6f on yielding ground a tall ask

runners_data.name: Inform
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride for G M Lyons on a lightly-raced debutant whose style and going suitability are both unknown — the trainer's 14-day stats (4 from 25) are reasonable but the complete absence of a form line demands caution in projection

runners_data.name: Keogie
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's prominent racer showed a clear best-effort when second over 6f at Heathpark and returns to that trip and similar going after 106 days off, making this a notable reappearance test where freshness is a double-edged sword

runners_data.name: Noble Irish
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan partners a first-time starter for Aidan O'Brien's operation with unknown style and going preferences — lightly-raced O'Brien juveniles/three-year-olds can arrive straight to winning but the intelligence vacuum makes probability assignment difficult

runners_data.name: Optics
runners_data.note: Ms McDowall's filly is a genuine hold-up type by nature but the crowded rear of this field means she is mapped further forward than she will actually race — her form over 5f and 6f on good ground is unimpressive (6th, 7th, 13th) and STYLE_FIT discount applies here

runners_data.name: Spider Star
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery rides a David Harry Kelly first-timer with no public form line, unknown style, and unknown going preferences — in a field of 17 with this many unknowns, debut runners from smaller operations face very steep odds against making an immediate impression

runners_data.name: Spinola Bear
runners_data.note: Ronan Whelan's hold-up type has twice raced on good ground and finished 7th and 17th — both efforts over 6-7f at Cork and elsewhere show no encouragement, and 33 days between runs does little to lift the profile

runners_data.name: Faithful Ardad
runners_data.note: Declan McDonogh steers another Kieran Cotter debutant alongside stablemate Haroussa — the complete absence of exposed form and the unknown style tag mean this runner must be treated with full opacity until it shows something on track

runners_data.name: Feel Happy
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's runner has a consistent profile of mid-single-digit finishes over 6-8f and the 37-day break may suit, with all three recorded efforts on good ground suggesting no going issue — the unknown style tag is the only material uncertainty in an otherwise readable profile

runners_data.name: Grande Cuvee
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan rides Stack's prominent-style filly who was second over 5f at Navan and third over 5f on good, and steps up to 6f here — the trip extension is a mild query but her consistent proximity to the pace on similar ground marks her as a realistic factor

runners_data.name: Haroussa
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners J P Murtagh's prominent type, but both career starts have come over a mile on good ground — dropping to 6f is a significant trip reduction and it is far from clear she has the pace to travel as prominently over this shorter distance

runners_data.name: Lilli's Angel
runners_data.note: Daniel McLoughlin's hold-up mare has finished 8th and 9th in her last two over 7-6f on good ground, and a fade-in-finish flag compounds the concern — 43 days off and no visible trajectory of improvement make this hard to elevate

runners_data.name: Otsana
runners_data.note: W J Lee takes the mount for P Twomey on one of the two confirmed pace-setters — Otsana's sole start was a creditable 5th over 7f on good and the step back to 6f on yielding ground suits the front-running profile, though sharing the lead in a field this size is a significant energy cost

runners_data.name: Red Dahlia
runners_data.note: Shane Foley is an obvious positive for John Joseph Murphy's debutant but the unknown style, unknown going preference, and absence of any form line place this runner firmly in the opaque category — the jockey quality alone cannot be converted into a meaningful probability

runners_data.name: Saint Agatha
runners_data.note: Gavin Ryan partners Stack's second runner, a confirmed front-runner who finished second over 7f at Gowran on good going and was second over 7f on good again — the 118-day absence is worth watching but she has clearly shown a willingness to race prominently and that role is confirmed here

runners_data.name: She's Too Kool
runners_data.note: Adam Browne-Souza's hold-up filly has solid course and distance form (4th and 6th over 6f at Cork on good going among eight similar-ground efforts) but has never won — she is a reliable place-sector type but the congested rear of the field may prevent her from finding daylight when it matters most

races.paceDynamic: Otsana and Saint Agatha are the two confirmed front-runners in a 17-runner maiden, and with both looking to establish a lead from the gates the early pace will be genuinely contested rather than controlled. On Good To Yielding ground at Cork over 6f, a brisk early duel between those two is likely to produce an honest, pressured gallop that stretches the field and drains finishing reserves from those going forward. With the field also containing prominent types such as Keogie, Grande Cuvee, and Haroussa who will be tracking close to the speed, the front rank will be under sustained pressure throughout, setting up conditions where those able to settle and produce a sustained run from midfield hold the clearest tactical advantage. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position — of those, Otsana and Saint Agatha are most likely to actually lock down the lead, with Keogie and Grande Cuvee forced to work harder than ideal to find a pitch just behind them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Midfield Finishers
scenarios.trigger: If Otsana and Saint Agatha fight for the lead and set a pressured gallop that burns out the front rank from the 2f pole
scenarios.body: The sustained duel up front on yielding ground will see the pace collapse inside the final furlong, handing the race to horses who settled in mid-division and produced a clean, progressive run

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pacemaker Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If one of Otsana or Saint Agatha blinks first and cedes the lead, allowing the other to bowl along at a controlled tempo
scenarios.body: A more measured gallop means the leader conserves enough energy to repel midfield challengers late, particularly on ground that rewards those who travel well within themselves

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong but not truly ruinous, and the prominent trackers time their challenge perfectly from just off the leaders
scenarios.body: Keogie and Grande Cuvee, both suited by 6f and capable on this type of ground, are ideally placed to exploit any slight easing of the lead and hit the line running

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace truly collapses and the field bunches, gifting ground to genuine hold-up horses with a strong late kick
scenarios.body: She's Too Kool has the course and distance form to theoretically benefit, but most hold-up types in this race are redistributed from their natural position and cannot fully exploit a true closing scenario

watchPoints.text: Otsana and Saint Agatha are on a collision course for the lead — if neither concedes in the first furlong the resulting duel on yielding ground could burn out both and dramatically compress the finish for midfield closers

Colin Keane on Inform for G M Lyons is a formidable booking for a debutant — watch the market move closely, as unexposed Lyons runners with elite jockey bookings frequently arrive with significant stable expectation
Grande Cuvee with Seamie Heffernan steps up from 5f to 6f and her best form came at 5f — monitor early how she travels off the strong pace, as the extra furlong on yielding ground is an open question

Keogie returns after 106 days off for Noel Meade — fresh horses in this stable can be underdone but the 6f trip and similar-going form (2nd at Heathpark) mark this as a significant return target if fit

She's Too Kool has the most course-and-distance experience of any runner in the field (multiple 6f runs at Cork on good ground) but has never won — in a wide-open maiden, consistent profile horses can finally break through, but so can debutants with hidden potential

races.name: Follow Us On Instagram Handicap

runners_data.name: Arch Enemy
runners_data.note: Progressive 7yo hold-up horse with two recent wins over 12f on Good; Sam Coen claim could be useful in a big field, and the soft-ish ground suits, though getting a clear passage from off the pace in a 21-runner field is the key logistical challenge.
runners_data.comment: Arch Enemy has distance and going experience to call on and her two wins in recent starts show she retains ability, but a fifth last time out and an unplaced effort two starts back suggest she finds the top end elusive under 140 lb.

runners_data.name: Forlio
runners_data.note: Genuine strong stayer who won over 12f on Good and has consistent form over this sort of trip; W J Lee a significant booking for T14-active trainer Paul Flynn, and a tongue-strap is fitted — naturally settles in rear so will need a clear run in a congested 21-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Forlio won three starts back but has found little since, finishing unplaced and fifth in his last two, and a trainer striking at just five per cent recently is a concern; he has run over today's trip and going, though 140 lb is a stiff enough burden.

runners_data.name: Glittering Gem
runners_data.note: Prominent-style 4yo for the powerful Weld yard, second over 10f and placed at 12f, both on Good; Chris Hayes is an excellent pilot in big-field handicaps and this step up to 14f looks the right move — best placed of all prominent types to exploit the pace battle on the front end.
runners_data.comment: Glittering Gem has shown enough consistency to hold interest, finishing second and third in recent starts, though she remains yet to win in her last five and a fourth last time out suggests she may struggle to bridge the gap from midfield; 140 lb is no help.

runners_data.name: Louiescall
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won over 16f on Good and has extensive course form; trainer T14 strike rate of 4/12 shows yard in form, but facing two other genuine pace horses means he will be contested early and must survive a war of attrition over the extra ground.
runners_data.comment: Louiescall showed he can win when landing first place three starts back, but he was unplaced last time and sixth two starts back, suggesting inconsistency; he has run over today's trip and going, and returns fit on a 14-day turnaround carrying 140 lb.

runners_data.name: Justenzia
runners_data.note: Hold-up 4yo whose best runs have come over 12-13f on Good; placed twice recently but has a habit of finding trouble in running, and a 31-day break for the Hogan yard — moderate T14 figures — gives no strong recency signal either way.
runners_data.comment: Justenzia has run over today's trip and going before and, with our rating putting her clear of most rivals, she shapes as a genuine threat despite carrying 138 lb; the main concern is her failure to convert in recent starts, leaving her winless in her last six.

runners_data.name: Morse
runners_data.note: Confirmed hold-up 6yo who fades in finishes — a notable concern over 14f with a strong pace; 80-day break and zero wins on similar ground in five attempts make this a difficult profile to back with confidence, and Charles Weld's stable has run cold (0/6 T14).
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and off the track for 80 days, Morse arrives short of recent form, though he has run over today's trip and going before and our rating nudges above his official mark — enough to keep him in the picture without inspiring outright confidence.

runners_data.name: Victoria Kesia
runners_data.note: Hold-up 5yo with experience over 16f at Galway on Good, though her three runs at that trip all resulted in finishes of 7th or worse; Gavin Ryan takes over and she has some soft-ground form, but the step to 14f has not yet produced a placing.
runners_data.comment: Victoria Kesia showed what she is capable of with a win five starts back, has experience over today's trip and going, and our rating of 76 puts her third among 21 rivals; the concern is a patchy recent record that includes an unseated rider in her last four outings.

runners_data.name: Dutch Gold
runners_data.note: Tall, hold-up 6yo who fades in finishes and is mapped to midfield because genuine closers are oversubscribed at the back; Noel Meade's yard has one win from 16 T14 runners and Dutch Gold's form figures of 0000 in 2025 give little confidence regardless of position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Dutch Gold nonetheless holds a clear edge on our rating over much of this field and brings distance and going experience to the table; the risk is that 69 days off and a consistent lack of recent impact make him difficult to trust.

runners_data.name: Questionable
runners_data.note: Holds a tongue-strap and is a natural hold-up type who won over 10f on Soft — his best ground profile — and placed at 12f; operating from midfield rather than his preferred deep-cover position reduces his chance, and 54 days off for a low-volume trainer warrants caution.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and 54 days since she last appeared, Questionable faces a stiff ask off 135 lb, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a rating of 72 suggests she holds a shade more ability than her official mark of 65 implies.

runners_data.name: Valjean
runners_data.note: Returning from a remarkable 682-day absence and wears a hood; last ran over 14f on Good in 2023 when last of 14, and Charles Weld's T14 record is 0/6 — the lack of recent racecourse evidence makes meaningful assessment almost impossible.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and absent for 682 days, Valjean faces a stiff comeback test, though he has run over today's trip and going before and carries 135 lb into a wide-open field where his speed rating of 82 offers faint encouragement.

runners_data.name: Rocket Robyn
runners_data.note: 4yo who fades in finishes and drops back from a staying trip; her best form has come over 9-10f on Softer ground, and the 14f trip on today's going looks a stretch — mapped to midfield rather than her preferred hold-up spot, compounding the concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 15 of 21 on our figures, Rocket Robyn is hard to fancy at the weights carrying 134 lb, though her recent second and prior distance experience offer slim crumbs of comfort after 49 days off.

runners_data.name: Eternal Echo
runners_data.note: 5yo hold-up type who has shown ability at 12-14f but form figures include U and multiple finishes outside the frame; David O'Sullivan's yard is 0/5 T14, and 69 days off plus question marks in the form book make this hard to assess with conviction.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and carrying 133 lb, Eternal Echo nevertheless holds a clear edge on ratings among these 21 rivals, and his experience over today's trip and going is a solid foundation; the recent unseating clouds the picture slightly, but he remains the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Guy's Girl
runners_data.note: 4yo hold-up filly whose one placing over 13f on Good is her chief asset; trainer McCreery has a solid T14 rate (3/13) and Keithen Kennedy's claim helps, but she is mapped into midfield rather than her natural position and has not threatened in six recent starts.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Guy's Girl does at least bring experience of today's distance and going, and her speed rating offers a shade of encouragement, though two unplaced efforts in a row and a mid-table ranking make this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Nancee Spain
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner wearing a hood, a winner over 12f on Soft and placed twice at 14f; has plenty of pace but her record shows she is vulnerable when the gallop is truly searching, and she will have Louiescall and Out On Friday for company throughout — survival to the line is the question.
runners_data.comment: Rated 63 by the handicapper and our rating of 70 suggests she holds a touch more ability than that, but four successive starts since her win have returned two fifths, a sixth and an eighth, making it hard to make a compelling case. Has experience of today's trip and going, though.

runners_data.name: Ohmali
runners_data.note: 4yo hold-up type placed over 8f on Good, but today's 14f trip looks significantly beyond her optimal range; Ben Coen is a top booking but even so, moving from midfield placement into contention over this extra ground is a tall ask given her distance profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Ohmali does bring going experience to the table and returns on a fresh enough 24-day break, but a modest official rating of 63 and a string of unplaced efforts make it hard to fancy him strongly from 14th in the rankings.

runners_data.name: Preparations
runners_data.note: Won last time over 12f on Good for the Slattery stable (trainer and jockey combination), and T14 figures of 3/14 show a yard firing; a hold-up type by nature but has winning form at 12f that projects plausibly to 14f — natural closer mapped into midfield, so needs to find its way to the rail for a clean passage.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 20 of 21 on our figures, Preparations is hard to fancy despite a win last time out; four of her last five starts have produced a sixth, an unplaced run, a seventh and a fourth, and she carries 133 lb into what looks a stiff task.

runners_data.name: Out On Friday
runners_data.note: 10yo front-runner with a win over 10f on Good and placed at 10f; Wesley Joyce's claim helps the weight, but as the third confirmed pace-setter in this race his role is likely to be pacemaker for others rather than winner — exposed at the top of his form cycle and vulnerable after a hard race if pressed from the front.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 16 of 21 on our figures, Out On Friday makes little appeal despite returning on a quick 12-day turnaround; a second five starts back is the sole encouragement, and experience over today's distance and going at least counts in his favour.

runners_data.name: Lauderdale King
runners_data.note: 4yo hold-up type placed at 10f on Good and dropping back from 13f; trainer/jockey combination of Andrew Slattery has strong T14 form (3/14) and the horse is lightly raced, but mapped away from his natural position and still a maiden at 4 — potential each-way curiosity rather than a leading candidate.
runners_data.comment: Lauderdale King has been winless in his last five starts, with only a single placing to show along the way, and ranked 17 of 21 on our figures he faces a stiff task here; experience over today's trip and going is about the best that can be said, with the 10-day turnaround at least suggesting he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Beauvallon
runners_data.note: High-quality 4yo for Willie Mullins, rated OR=71 (top of the field), with two wins over 16f and a second over 17f — stamina is emphatically proven; T14 rate of 7/32 is moderate for the yard but the step back to 14f suits a horse who travels well, and this profile — stayer with class — is ideally suited to being gifted the race by a pace collapse.
runners_data.comment: Beauvallon is yet to win in his last four starts, though a fourth three starts back hints at some ability and he arrives unexposed and open to improvement; a trainer striking at 29% in the past fortnight is a positive angle.

runners_data.name: Charlie Brow'n
runners_data.note: 6yo with a win over 14f on Soft and placed at 12f in recent form; no jockey listed and 9 days since last run is tight, but trainer O'Mara's yard is 0/4 T14 — a natural closer who will find himself racing in a midfield berth rather than deep cover in this strongly-run 21-runner race.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 18 of 21 on our figures, Charlie Brow'n makes a tough ask at 130 lb, and a seventh two starts back sits deep in a patchy recent spell; he has run over today's trip and going, and a third last time out offers a slim crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Miss Australie
runners_data.note: 5yo who won over 14f on Good at her most recent start just three days ago — an extremely quick turnaround; Adrian McGuinness is 3/21 T14, and while she clearly goes on Good ground and the trip suits, the very short recovery from her last run is the dominant risk factor here.
runners_data.comment: Miss Australie won last time out but ranks 19th of 21 on our figures, making her hard to fancy at the weights — 136 lb is a stiff burden — though she has run over today's trip and going before and arrives fit on a three-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Louiescall, Nancee Spain, and Out On Friday are all confirmed front-runners in a 21-runner field over 1m4f on Good To Yielding ground at Cork, making a strong, sustained gallop a near-certainty from the outset. These three will press each other throughout the early and middle stages, meaning fractions will be honest to strong and the race will function as a genuine stamina test rather than a tactical affair. The prolonged pace battle risks emptying the leaders late, creating a scenario where horses travelling smoothly just off the pace — particularly those with proven stamina at this trip and beyond — are positioned to pick up the pieces. This race shape firmly favours the prominent-to-midfield racer with a strong staying profile and the ability to quicken off a true pace; pure hold-up horses face an additional complication, as the field contains far more genuine hold-up types than can realistically settle towards the rear — Beauvallon, Forlio, Arch Enemy, and Glittering Gem are among those most likely to secure a workable position, while the deepest closers will be shuffled further back than ideal and may find the pace evens out before they can land a blow.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way pace battle between Louiescall, Nancee Spain, and Out On Friday burns them all out turning for home, leaving the race to resolute mid-track travellers.
scenarios.body: The sustained duel drains the front-runners over the final quarter-mile, and horses racing within a length or two of the pace without expending energy take command; Good To Yielding ground amplifies the cost of early exertion, rewarding those with natural stamina who covered ground economically.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pacesetter Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners — most plausibly Louiescall — establishes a slight advantage and finds enough stamina reserves to hold the stalkers at bay.
scenarios.body: Louiescall has course form over 2m and a strong record on Good ground, and if the pace is honest but not suicidal — perhaps Out On Friday or Nancee Spain falters first — a single horse can control tempo and husband enough energy for a late kick.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly blistering and the field spreads wide, creating a clear late lane for a horse sweeping from well off the pace.
scenarios.body: Beauvallon, with a proven staying profile over 2m and strong form on this surface, has the quality to exploit late gaps if ridden patiently, and Forlio's course-and-distance form supports a late flourish; however, several redistributed hold-up types will be competing for the same late real estate, diluting the impact of any single closer.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Muddle, Midfield Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the large field of 21 causes early positional chaos, leaders slow fractionally, and the race resolves into a bunch finish favouring a prominent horse with a sharp turn of foot.
scenarios.body: With jockeys managing traffic in a packed field, tempo could fluctuate before the final bend, allowing a horse racing in the top six to quicken away; Glittering Gem for Weld and Preparations, who won last time out, are best placed to exploit a messy, uneven gallop from a handy berth.

watchPoints.text: Beauvallon (Mullins, OR=71) is the classiest horse in the race and has two wins over 16f — if the three-way pace battle between Louiescall, Nancee Spain, and Out On Friday burns them out, Beauvallon is perfectly equipped to swoop late.

Glittering Gem represents the Weld yard with Chris Hayes aboard and is the most naturally positioned prominent horse to benefit from a true pace — watch how Hayes slots her in the first four early, as that berth could be decisive.

Miss Australie ran only three days ago — watch market move carefully; if heavily supported despite the quick turnaround she must be respected given the 14f win form, but if the market is cold it signals connections are managing the schedule rather than targeting this race.

Valjean (682 days off, Charles Weld) is a complete unknown on return and wears a hood — watch paddock closely for signs of freshness or over-exuberance that could compromise what is already a very difficult comeback profile.

With 21 runners and three genuine front-runners, positioning at the start will be critical — watch for a cluster of hold-up horses getting checked or bumped entering the first bend, which could compromise the chances of several runners before the race has properly begun.
